requirements.text: HRC0000711 was requested for Tabitha Bullock but by mistake they used Christina Oliver instead of Tabitha Bullock so we have to correct this
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 1 AND opened_for = 3
assumptions: case HRC0000711 is hr_case_id 1, opened for hr_profile 2 (Christina Oliver)
opened_for references hr_profile; Tabitha Bullock is user 3 with hr_profile 3, the only person of that name
'requested for' is the subject employee, opened_for; opened_by is not named by the request and is not tested

requirements.text: We had to Verify Home address and to update the emergency contacts for case HRC0000711 which is done. So please close the tasks
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE parent_case = 1 AND status = 'closed_complete'
assumptions: case 1 has exactly two tasks on the seed, Verify Home Address (1) and Update Emergency Contacts (2), both draft, the two the request names
'which is done' makes the closed state closed_complete rather than closed_incomplete

requirements.text: propose solution to the affected person
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 1 AND status = 'awaiting_acceptance'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: proposing a solution leaves the case awaiting the employee's acceptance; the seed's open solution_proposal notifications carry that status
the case is in draft; the policy reaches awaiting_acceptance only through work_in_progress, so the final state needs two transitions

requirements.text: propose solution to the affected person
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 1 AND email = 'tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com' AND type = 'solution_proposal'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (61 after 60); one notification is created
the affected person is Tabitha Bullock, for whom the case was requested
type solution_proposal: the notification type for proposing a solution in this system

email kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy: it is Tabitha Bullock's user email, the address the listed user lookup returns; every seed notification goes to hr_profile.personal_email instead (tabitha.bullock.3@personal.example.com), but no listed tool reads hr_profile
notification status and org_id not fixed by request or policy and not tested

disagreement: email: A IN ('tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com', 'tabitha.bullock.3@personal.example.com'), B 'tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com'; chose the user email because the benchmark check is the prior and neither the request, the policy nor the seed contradicts it; the seed's personal-address convention does not, since no listed tool returns that address

requirements.text: propose solution to the affected person
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE hr_case_id = 1 AND type = 'solution_proposal' AND email LIKE '%christina.oliver%'
assumptions: boundary of 'the affected person': Christina Oliver, the case's current, mistaken subject, receives no solution proposal for it at either of her addresses

disagreement: email: A IN ('christina.oliver@carsonllc.com', 'christina.oliver.2@personal.example.com'), B LIKE '%christina.oliver%'; chose the LIKE predicate because it covers both of her addresses and any other spelling of them, so the stay fails in every case the exact list catches and more

Send Notification.evidence: the check's work address tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com is Tabitha Bullock's user email; the request names the person, not an address, and the policy fixes none, so the benchmark's address stands. disagreement: disposition: A repaired (either her user or her personal email accepted, after the seed's notifications, all to personal addresses), B kept; chose kept because the seed convention does not contradict the check: no listed tool reads hr_profile, so the user email is the address an agent can reach

notes:
disagreement: value: the solution proposal's recipient address: one pass accepts Tabitha Bullock's user or personal email, the other only the user email the benchmark tests; kept the user email (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the predicate of the stay that Christina Oliver gets no solution proposal: one pass lists her two addresses exactly, the other matches any address containing her name; kept the second, which is tighter for a count that must stay at zero (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: disposition: Send Notification: repaired in one pass, kept in the other; chose kept (resolved in its evidence).
The two passes otherwise agree on every row, id and cell.
The case status requirement is implied rather than stated: the request asks only to close the tasks and propose a solution, and the benchmark tests awaiting_acceptance, the state a proposed solution waits in.
Every seed notification is addressed to a personal email from hr_profile, whereas the benchmark expects Tabitha Bullock's work email; no listed tool reads hr_profile, so the work email returned by the user lookup is kept.
opened_by (also Christina Oliver's profile) is left untested: the request says the case was requested for Tabitha Bullock, which is opened_for, and the requester was the Service Desk.
The policy's lifecycle rules are written for cases; the tasks move from draft straight to closed_complete, which the request asks for. They are already inactive on the seed, and their active flag is not fixed by request or policy and is not tested.
The acting user Robin Monroe holds the manager role in org 1, which covers case and task updates.
